[ASSISTANT_SAID] Studies indicate that cultural competency training can positively impact the healthcare experience for West Indian immigrants, improving knowledge, skills, and patient satisfaction.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] A study published in the Journal of the American Board of Family Medicine found that cultural competency training improved primary care physicians' knowledge and skills.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Another study published in the Journal of Health Care for the Poor and Underserved found that cultural competency training decreased healthcare disparities and improved patient satisfaction among minority patients, including West Indian immigrants.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Cultural competency training is part of a larger effort to address the challenges faced by West Indian immigrants in accessing healthcare and social services.
